newsitem.title: USA: Compaq unveils new Presario PC line, in software pacts.
newsitem.headline: Compaq unveils new Presario PC line, in software pacts.

text.p: Compaq Computer Corp. Monday unveiled a new line of Presario home computers with prices that start under $1,000, and said it formed alliances with four software companies to sell personal computers in schools.
The Houston-based company said the new computer line includes eight Presario systems and two notebooks.

The less-expensive products include the new Presario 2200, which starts at a price of $799 with a 180 MHz Media GX processor. When purchased with a monitor, consumers can buy the total system for about $999.
The new Presario 4504, with a minitower design and an Intel Corp. Pentium 200 MHz processor, starts at $999 without a monitor, the company said.
The Presario 4504, 4508 and 4528 range in price from $999 to $1,899 and are expected to be available at nationwide retail stores in July.

The Presario 4808, 4814 and 4824 range in price from $1,999 to $2,699 and also will be available in July. These computers include a creativity imaging centre, home theatre surround sound, DVD, Pentium II processors and backlit easy access buttons, Compaq said.
The features of the notebooks, the 1200 and 1600 series, include Intel pentium chips with MMX multimedia technology and an eight-hour "DisqPlay" for music CDs, the company said.

Compaq said it entered alliances with Apple Computer Inc.'s Claris Corp., CUC International Inc.'s Davidson & Associates, Citadel Technology Inc. and McAfee Associates, as well as continuing its agreement with Roger Wagner Publishing Inc.
Compaq said in a statement that it will integrate the companies' software into a Presario ES personal computer aimed at schools with a price starting at $1,799.
Compaq said it will add a number of PC models for sale to schools, starting with the Presario 1090ES notebook, the first portable computer to be offered through its education programme.
Compaq's stock rose 44 cents to $98.81 on the New York Stock Exchange shortly after midday.
